IronMac: The Finish Line

By: Floris Kotze | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
The day of reckoning for Macfarlane, waiting for the gun on the start line for the 2023 Ironman challenge....

Unique Selling Point:
Anything is possible.
This is part 2 of Mac's Ironman challenge. We hear what it takes to finish the Ironman, not only physically but mentally too.

The day of reckoning. Mac is in PE and we spend the day with him doing Ironman.
We start the insert with a quick re-cap of the previous story of Mac training and the progress he’s made. His coach updates us on his condition, but the question remains:
Is he ready for the biggest challenge of his life?
Carte Blanche is in PE to find out.
Top SA Ironman Bradley Weiss (IRONMAN African Championship 2022 – 2nd Place Pro Male) has agreed to be interviewed. He will tell us exactly what it takes, and what Mac is going to face.
I am also looking to speak to a Sports Psychologist to give us the rundown on the mental toughness needed to do this.
We got permission from IronMan SA to film in designated areas, IronMan Operations Director Paul Wolff has agreed to give you access to the following areas on race day: Swim start, Transition, Finish line.
Big Shot Media has also agreed to assist us with some footage. They will have a full crew on the day.
Derek will support Mac and will be on the sidelines urging him on. We will feel the pain, the emotions and the elation through the eyes of Derek.
We will tell a parallel story as Mac is doing IronMan. To break the monotony of running and cycling, we will disperse interviews as Mac progresses throughout the day. At the center of this story, Mac’s promise to André.
We will build to a crescendo as Mac finishes his toughest challenge yet. Expect blood, sweat and a lot of tears.


Summary:
Derek spends the day with Mac, as he competes in the Ironman. We see first hand what it takes to do Ironman. We hear from pro athletes and Sports Psychologists.

Further information:
As we follow Mac's progress, we add in interviews throughout the day, we tell a parallel storyline to break the monotony of Ironman.

Extra Budget Items:
Traveling to PE, and accommodation. I have spoken to Denis Goddard to do camerawork for us for the day, but I have heard that we might have to reconsider him.

TX Date:


0000-00-00

Script:



Montage of Accidents, cyclists killed, chaos…
A driver allegedly struck and killed a cyclist on a pavement in Johannesburg
As a cyclist he died…
Derek
Right here I guess your life changed?
Mac:
It did Derek,
I was driving down this road and what I saw on the side of the road was a picture that will stick in my mind for the rest of my life.
Mac:
I always tease André, I said to him, why are you doing Ironman, what is wrong with you? And I said to him, you know what, when I'm old and stupid enough like you, I'll do Iron Man.
I am doing this Iron Man in honour of André, in honour of his memory, his kids, his wife…
Sharon:
It's an incredible gift that you can leave that somebody was impacted by André’s life and that, that light continues to shine through. That's why for me, it is something that I absolutely celebrate and applaud, because I'm going, that's what is so important, it is how André lived this life.
LINK: Our story starts here on the streets of Vereeniging, near the Vaal River. Where a young boy once roamed the streets and leading a carefree existence. Well that boy is now a grown man, trying to make a difference…
VO: To explain why this person is so special, we will need the help of someone who knows him well.
Derek:
This is the queen…. Qu een Florence how are you?
I am good and you?
VO:
And who better to tell us more about Macfarlane, than his Mom, Florence Moleli.
Derek:
And it's so good to meet the mother of Mac
Derek:
When did he tell you that he was going to do the Iron Man?
Mom:
It was surprised, it was a surprise, I did not believe it when he tells me about Ironman, yoh I have never never seen you on your bike, I have never seen you running, he said Mom, I'm going to show you!
VO:
He loved all sports, and whenever he showed interest in a subject, he was 100% committed.
Mom:
He wanted something that challenges him, he becomes easily bored so if the thing doesn't challenge him, he becomes bored and leaves it. He wants to achieve whatever he wants!
VO: And it was no more evident, than in a race he did back in December in preparation for Iron man. Although it was half the distance of a Full Iron Man, he missed the cut off time, but finished the race regardless.
Dr:
People want to test their limits always. The human being wants to see how far they can go. People will maybe tell you: it's impossible and you still believe I want to do that, it is something that drives me, can I go better can I go bigger. And that is part of the human spirit I believe.
VO: Dr Henning Gericke, is a clinical and sport psychologist, he has worked with many of our national sports teams, including the world cup winning Springboks, in 2007. He offers some sound advice to Mac…
Derek: Mac makes this promise to Andre and decide he's gonna do Ironman, what would you tell him 6 months when it's a better next year?

Dr:
I'll tell you why they don't do it just rather leave it no, just joking, the story of Andre is such a powerful story, making the promise, I want to do it, there's gonna be tough times during that race that you gonna feel is it worthwhile? That combination is the ideal for me to test the human mind and the human body.

Derek:
Mac, do you worry why you took this on in the first place?
Mac:
I don't I really don't, I think it's probably one of the best decisions I've ever made in my life, it’s been a total transformation for me, psychologically, physically. We’ve put in a lot of work there's been many people that have been behind us, from sponsors, to supporters. I don't want to let myself down first but I certainly don't want to let them down either.
Welcome to Nelson Mandela Bay…
VO: IronMan is one of the toughest sporting events in the world, it consists of a 3.8km swim, 180 km cycle and 42.2 km run.


Bradley:
Usually if you isolate any one of those three, you would be quite happy with your day's work and and go and put your feet up and have a beer. To put them all together and it's it's a bit of a crazy thing.
VO: Top South African Triathlete, Bradley Weiss, 2nd in this year’s IRONMAN African Championship, shared with us what it means to be an Ironman.
Bradley:
Everyone's on their own journey to that finish line and once they get there, it's just a very fulfilling and an overwhelming experience, to cross that finish line, and I think you know, why are we alive what are we doing this for, and being able to tick boxes like this, is definitely gives a bit of meaning to your days.
VO: Competitors have a total of 17 hours, to complete the full Ironman.
Derek Link:
Kenako, it is time for the Ironman African championship and our Macfarlane is in the starting blocks, he can't wait to get going.
VO: After only 6 months of training, Mac is facing an enormous challenge.
Derek:
Mac I can see you are ready for this?
Mac:
I am I really am. I don’t want to lie. I'm looking forward to this.
We’ll be with you all the way… thank you.
VO:
It was off to a good start for Mac, after the swim was shortened to 900m due to stormy weather. He took 22 minutes to finish the swim, then it was onto the bike for a gruelling 180km.
Mac:
As tough as it is, it is enjoyable to see people on the road cheering us on, hopefully that will get us to the finish line…
VO: Mac completed the first 90km in just over 4 hours. But, on the second lap, his pace dropped dramatically…
Bradley:
Those who can sort of keep in mind as fresh and focused and concentrated as possible, are normally the ones they come out on top. Can he complete it? Absolutely, I mean it depends how deep he wants to dig.


VO:
For the first time during this event, Mac was not smiling, it was clear that the cycling took its toll on his legs. His projected times to complete the Ironman had slipped, and were now outside of the cut off time at midnight. He would have to dig very deep to become an Ironman.

Mac completed the cycle in 9 hours 20. But. He was clearly suffering.

Derek: You've done bloody well so far Mac!
Mac: 180 km 42 more to go.
Derek: Is there much left in the tank here?
Mac: I don't know, I don't know
Derek: Come on Mac you can still do it man!
Mac: Okay.
Montage
Link: It's 10:10 and the streets are virtually deserted. It's 15 hours since Mac took to the water. This is some challenge, I can tell you that!
Mac: I've never been in so much pain! I just need to finish. I'm here to do what I came to do. It is really tough. The four most important words right now in my life will be: you are an IronMan, I can't wait to get to the finish line.
VO: With the cut off now within minutes, Mac did the impossible. He picked up the pace.
VO: Through sheer determination, Mac, the Ironman, crossed the finish line in 16 hours.
Mac:
Sharon and the kids…. Sharon, I am going to bring this home to you so you can see it. I think he was with me there…. You’ve changed my life forever!

TEASER ONE
VO: It was a promise made to his friend and cyclist Andre…
UPSOUND: Andre was a friend and cyclists killed on the road…
VO: Now, our very Macfarlane Moleli has completed one of the toughest challenges in the world – IronMan!

TEASER TWO
VO: It comprises a 3.8km swim, a 180 km cycle and a 42 km run… the Iron Man is one of the toughest challenges in the world…
UPSOUND:
VO: -Macfarlane puts his training to the ultimate test…

TEASER THREE
VO: It’s one of the most unforgiving long-distance triathlon races in the world… a 3.8km swim in icy waters, a 180 km cycle and a 42 km run…
UPSOUND MACFARLANE:
VO: Now, fulfilling a promise to his friend and cyclist, Macfarlane conquers the IronMan challenge…



VO:
Mac finally crossed the finish line in 16 hours, and was officially crowned, and Ironman!
VO: After witnessing the death of his friend and fellow triathlete, André Piehl, Mac made a promise to take up the challenge of tackling Ironman on the 5th March 2023, in an effort to bring more awareness to cycling safety on our roads.

VO: After witnessing the death of his friend and fellow triathlete, André Piehl, Mac made a promise to take up the challenge of tackling Ironman on the 5th March 2023, in an effort to bring more awareness to cycling safety on our roads.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): The day of reckoning for Macfarlane, waiting for the gun on the start line for the 2023 Ironman challenge....
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Anything is possible. This is part 2 of Mac's Ironman challenge. We hear what it takes to finish the Ironman, not only physically but mentally too. The day of reckoning. Mac is in PE and we spend the day with him doing Ironman. We start the insert with a quick re-cap of the previous story of Mac training and the progress he’s made. His coach updates us on his condition, but the question remains: Is he ready for the biggest challenge of his life? Carte Blanche is in PE to find out. Top SA Ironman Bradley Weiss (IRONMAN African Championship 2022 – 2nd Place Pro Male) has agreed to be interviewed. He will tell us exactly what it takes, and what Mac is going to face. I am also looking to speak to a Sports Psychologist to give us the rundown on the mental toughness needed to do this. We got permission from IronMan SA to film in designated areas, IronMan Operations Director Paul Wolff has agreed to give you access to the following areas on race day: Swim start, Transition, Finish line. Big Shot Media has also agreed to assist us with some footage. They will have a full crew on the day. Derek will support Mac and will be on the sidelines urging him on. We will feel the pain, the emotions and the elation through the eyes of Derek. We will tell a parallel story as Mac is doing IronMan. To break the monotony of running and cycling, we will disperse interviews as Mac progresses throughout the day. At the center of this story, Mac’s promise to André. We will build to a crescendo as Mac finishes his toughest challenge yet. Expect blood, sweat and a lot of tears.
metadata.Summary: Derek spends the day with Mac, as he competes in the Ironman. We see first hand what it takes to do Ironman. We hear from pro athletes and Sports Psychologists.
metadata.Further information: As we follow Mac's progress, we add in interviews throughout the day, we tell a parallel storyline to break the monotony of Ironman.
metadata.Extra Budget Items: Traveling to PE, and accommodation. I have spoken to Denis Goddard to do camerawork for us for the day, but I have heard that we might have to reconsider him.
